pillar_reactions.evidence: He tied it straight to his own stated need and then demonstrated he already understood the distinction being sold: 'I'm glad you mentioned that the training and, okay, mobility program, I need this, yeah. This is a key aspect of overall fitness.' When the rep said people confuse mobility and flexibility, the prospect finished the thought himself — 'Mobility, strength through range of motion, flexibility. Flexibility is just stretching the muscle to make it longer.' He had also pre-sold himself on the modality earlier: 'kettlebell made so much of a difference... my body is able to catch on to what's happening with the movement. This is something I don't see with dumbbells or doing bands.'

The only pillar he interrupted for. 'I'm not sure if this stuff is scientifically proven or not... I see a lot of fitness influencers speaking about diet based on blood groups. And I'm not sure if that's a thing, but if that helps me, I can probably get some tests done to know what I should be eating.' He was asking whether the programme includes diagnostic testing and got a deferral to Trevor rather than an answer.

Delivered with the personal cell number, the over-communication instruction and the community, and the whole reaction was 'Okay.' Notable because this is the pillar he had pre-named as his requirement twenty minutes earlier — 'I want to be able to give you like a weekly report of what I'm doing... accountability. And that's what I mentioned earlier also. And I need this.' The pillar that mattered most to him drew the least reaction, because the rep delivered it as a monologue rather than tying it back to the words the prospect had already given him.

anchors.raw: she was so obsessed with this that to the point where she quit her job for a year and she just focused on her health. I think she's down maybe a good 18, 16 or 18 kilos.
anchors.note: The strongest supportive anchor in this batch. His wife joined a CrossFit box, joined a gym, systematically attends classes with every coach within a radius, and gave up a year of income for her health. The household has already decided that paid coaching and lost earnings are acceptable costs for this outcome, which makes a $4,000 line item unremarkable. The rep noticed the inspiration angle — 'it seems like your wife's a bit of an inspiration' — but never used it as a price frame.

anchors.raw: there's a thing about Trevor, and the way he's trying to mentor people through his posts, where I feel he's not another, you know, bullshitter, influencer, just trying to flex his muscles and trying to sell a program... just hearing him speak gives me the confidence that I can completely believe him, 10-on-10.
anchors.note: He arrived pre-sold on the practitioner and volunteered a 10/10 unprompted. Trust was never the constraint on this call; scheduling was. Worth noting for attribution that the entire trust anchor was built by organic Instagram content before any rep contact.

anchors.raw: I've gotten a few memberships over the years, and I've barely made it over a week. So I'm just not consistent.
anchors.note: His entire purchase history in this category is cheap memberships he abandoned inside a week. That is the reference class a $4,000 commitment has to clear, and it is also the honest basis for his own risk — he is not sceptical of the programme, he is sceptical of himself. The rep never asked what those memberships cost, so the numeric anchor was never surfaced.

anchors.raw: So I've only met two personal coaches over the past decade... Partly because everyone I speak with wants me to commit to a time, you know, the very first meeting.
anchors.note: Two in-person coach conversations in ten years, both in a low-cost local market, both of which ended over scheduling rather than price. No figure was ever stated, so this is a modality anchor more than a price anchor, but it is the comparison set he is working from.

unmet_demand.want: A programme that survives a genuinely unpredictable airline roster — 2 a.m. starts, 12-hour duty days, no fixed availability from one week to the next
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asserted flexibility and a 30-minute session length, which is a real answer to time cost but not to unpredictability. Nobody addressed what happens to a three-to-four-session week when he is awake at 2 a.m. four days running, and no adherence expectation was set against that. The single most likely reason this close does not survive to month three, and it was left unvalidated.

unmet_demand.want: To know what equipment he actually needs before starting — how many kettlebells, what weights, whether anything else is required
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised it explicitly as one of two things he needed — 'I still need to understand equipment. Is it just a kettlebell or, you know, how many do I need to make available for myself?' — and it was never answered on the call. He bought without knowing what he has to acquire, and he trains in a small apartment building gym.

Asked directly and deferred: 'that's a question that I would say, save it for Trevor. Initially, we're not going to recommend you that, but as we progress, it could be a possibility.' The underlying premise he raised — blood-group-based dieting — is not evidence-based, and the answer neither corrected it nor closed it off, leaving him expecting testing may come later.

unmet_demand.want: Weight and muscle gain as a lifelong hardgainer who loses 1-2 kg of water in a session and does not eat when tired
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He named gaining size three separate times and named the specific mechanism he fears — 'the more I work out, the more tired I get. And when I'm tired, I usually don't eat.' The nutrition pillar was delivered generically around baseline diet, restrictions, supplementation and fasting, with fasting emphasised for over-40s, which points in the opposite direction from his goal. Nobody positioned the programme against surplus eating for a hardgainer.
